entry.title: Streaming Background Of Financial Technology And Smart Contracts 0C2B748761
entry.summary: Background of Financial Technology and Smart Contracts reports that FinTech smart-contract research concentrates on security, scalability, legal-regulatory, privacy, and latency challenges, with proposed solutions still far from effective. This independently corresponds to Kaal's identification of regulatory uncertainty around blockchain and smart contracts, while showing that the uncertainty sits among broader technical constraints. The proposition does not establish that legal frameworks worldwide must change.

entry.title: Streaming From Stack To Structure A9551E4269
entry.summary: From stack to structure reports that Ethereum's general-purpose EVM enabled rapid development of a decentralized-application ecosystem implemented through smart contracts. This independently corresponds to Kaal's account of Ethereum as a platform on which developers can build applications directly. entry.title: Streaming The Dark Side Of Smart Contracts A Contract Theory Perspective 9753E68539
entry.summary: The Dark Side of Smart Contracts states that smart contracts may govern transactions more cheaply than traditional contracts, firm hierarchies, and relational contracts. This independently corresponds to Kaal's Coasean account of smart contracts as a lower-cost substitute for firm organization. The proposition is qualified and does not establish minimal costs for transactions of every size or high transaction security.

entry.summary: An ontology-driven approach to security analysis of Sui Move smart contracts argues that mature Ethereum tools often detect syntactic vulnerabilities while missing divergences between intended design and on-chain implementation, leaving functionality open to manipulation. entry.summary: An ontology-driven approach to security analysis of Sui Move smart contracts states that attackers exploit smart-contract vulnerabilities to steal large sums and that defensive methodologies have developed in response. entry.title: Streaming Beyond Traditional Contracts Smart Contracts And The Transformation Of Indian Co 9648849F03
entry.summary: Beyond Traditional Contracts reports that the legal status of smart contracts in Indian commercial law remains doctrinally fragmented. This independently supplies an India-specific instance of the regulatory uncertainty Kaal identifies around blockchain and smart contracts. The proposition does not establish the condition of financial-services law globally or prove that every jurisdiction must change its framework.

entry.title: Streaming Ai Tokenomics And The Firm 9Cba1Df1C1
entry.summary: AI Tokenomics and the Firm describes generative AI as lowering the cost of prediction, language, and code generation. This independently corresponds to Kaal's marginal-cost-collapse mechanism for abundant digital realizations. The abstract proposition does not establish that marginal cost reaches zero, that supply becomes horizontal, or that pricing shifts entirely to generative capacity.

entry.title: Streaming Quantitative Cooperation Analysis Among Cross Chain Smart Contracts Bdc65A0813
entry.summary: Quantitative Cooperation Analysis among Cross-chain Smart Contracts reports that numerous cooperating smart contracts form a complex interaction network that is difficult to evaluate. This independently corresponds to Kaal's premise that multi-party smart-contract arrangements create distinctive complexity, while qualifying the suggestion that blockchain infrastructure alone makes the arrangement sufficiently verifiable. The abstract does not establish whether the proposed evaluation method is unhackable.

entry.title: Streaming On Observing Contracts Deontic Contracts Meet Smart Contracts 112E63A687
entry.summary: On Observing Contracts identifies a semantic gap through which smart-contract behavior can diverge from intended deontic behavior. This independently supports the mechanism in Kaal's claim that code and natural-language logic differ in ways that can frustrate human intent. The abstract proposition does not establish that this divergence occurs across all smart-contract settings.

entry.title: Streaming All Smart Contracts Are Ambiguous 7Ef107D3Ee
entry.summary: All Smart Contracts Are Ambiguous argues that technical facts can depend on socially determined facts, so smart-contract code can remain ambiguous. This independently qualifies the idea that code eliminates interpretive uncertainty and corresponds to Kaal's concern about how courts interpret coded agreements. The proposition does not specify Kaal's reasonable-human interpretive test or a particular legal doctrine.

entry.title: Streaming Adaptive Tokenomics A Systems Engineering Approach To Programmable Incentive Des 6De14552B1
entry.summary: Adaptive Tokenomics argues that token projects lack an established field integrating economics, control theory, game theory, and constitutional design. This independently corresponds to Kaal's claim that productive decentralized networks require dynamic design, checks and balances, and game-theoretic incentives. The proposition is a field-level diagnosis, not evidence that any particular design keeps a network productive.

entry.title: Streaming Do Smart Contracts Incur Higher Transaction Costs Than Traditional Contracts 4112Fa0866
entry.summary: Do Smart Contracts Incur Higher Transaction Costs than Traditional Contracts? argues that adapting institutional arrangements can cause smart contracts to incur higher transaction costs than traditional contracts. This directly challenges Kaal's proposition that smart contracting removes almost all transaction costs. The abstract frames the result as a possibility grounded in transaction-cost economics and does not provide an empirical cost estimate.

entry.title: Streaming End To End Smart Legal Contracts 4Cf27D6C1C
entry.summary: End-to-End Smart Legal Contracts argues that smart contracts need a firm private-law foundation before regulation is considered. This independently corresponds to Kaal's sequencing claim that contract-law doctrine must be adjusted before smart contracts are fully accommodated. The abstract proposition does not identify which formation, interpretation, conditions, or remedies rules require adjustment.

entry.summary: Interpretation of Contracts and Smart Contracts distinguishes deterministic computer language, in which one meaning and result are contemplated, from natural language, which remains open to multiple meanings. This independently supports the language-logic mechanism in Kaal's claim about smart-contract interpretation. The proposition does not by itself establish that smart contracts cannot accommodate human business interaction in every setting.

entry.title: Streaming Smart Contracts As Execution Instead Of Expression 9Cddad2A73
entry.summary: Smart Contracts as Execution Instead of Expression argues that human-readable contractual terms, interpretation, and contract-law correction help make execution conform to party expectations. That independently corresponds to Kaal's insistence on human-readable terms and interpretive flexibility alongside code. The abstract proposition does not establish Kaal's proposed Codex rule or the specific common-law mutual-understanding standard.

entry.title: Streaming Legal Regulation Of Artificial Intelligence International Experience 4E1Acced5A
entry.summary: Legal regulation of artificial intelligence: international experience argues prospectively that European AI and robotics standards will support industry development while ensuring human-rights compliance. That assessment qualifies Kaal's warning that strict AI regulation may stifle innovation by presenting standards as potentially development-supporting. The proposition is normative and forward-looking, not an observed industry effect, and it is not limited to legal AI applications.

entry.title: Streaming Artificial Intelligence Governance And Regulation A Roadmap To Developin 50Ed4B8D1A
entry.summary: Artificial Intelligence Governance and Regulation states that the more lenient United States approach promotes innovation but produces legal ambiguity. This independently corresponds to the lenient-regulation side of Kaal's two-sided legal-AI governance tradeoff. The source identifies ambiguity, not unchecked bias, as the cost, so it qualifies rather than duplicates Kaal's consequence and does not establish causation from the abstract alone.

entry.title: Streaming Artificial Intelligence Governance And Regulation A Roadmap To Developin 36A75A6E9D
entry.summary: Artificial Intelligence Governance and Regulation reports that stringent EU-style regulation can improve legal clarity and public trust while raising compliance costs and hindering innovation. This corresponds to the strict-regulation side of Kaal's two-sided legal-AI governance tradeoff and qualifies it by identifying claimed benefits alongside innovation costs. The abstract calls the support empirical but does not expose the design or permit causal inference.

entry.title: Streaming Artificial Intelligence Regulation Approaches And Implications D28Af22Ee5
entry.summary: Artificial Intelligence Regulation: Approaches and Implications argues that rapidly evolving AI technology and threats require specifically adapted regulation. This supports the pacing diagnosis in Kaal's claim that static frameworks cannot keep pace with technological innovation. entry.title: Streaming Legal Regulation Of Artificial Intelligence C8Dac61Ac2
entry.summary: Legal Regulation of Artificial Intelligence argues that an AI application should be classified as high risk when it can significantly affect individuals and prohibited when incompatible with fundamental rights. This independently corresponds to Kaal's account of fundamental-rights exposure as the basis for high-risk treatment under the EU AI Act. The abstract proposition is broader than judicial proceedings and does not establish the specific transparency, bias-audit, or human-oversight requirements in Kaal's claim.

entry.title: Streaming No Accounting For Corporate Governance Proxy Voting With Securities Lend 8E8Afa8E63
entry.summary: No accounting for corporate governance identifies a concrete proxy-voting failure: voting rights were not tracked when securities were lent, leading to improper vote counts. This extends Kaal's requirement that voting systems count votes robustly and transparently by showing that entitlement tracking is part of accurate counting. The evidence concerns corporate proxy voting, not quadratic voting or DAO manipulation.

entry.title: Streaming Dao And Tokenized Governance The Problem Of Decentralized Decision Makin Bb04F5297E
entry.summary: DAO and tokenized governance treats decentralization as a measurement problem and proposes criteria based on minimum independent decision centers and the relationship among protocol, users, and developers. That framework qualifies Kaal's hierarchy-centered account of decentralization by identifying additional dimensions that a metric may need to capture. The proposition is conceptual and normative, not an empirical validation of either metric.

entry.title: Streaming A Meta Analysis Of Corporate Governance And Firm Performance Da81Eb9623
entry.summary: A meta-analysis of corporate governance and firm performance reports that stronger governance indices and greater board independence are associated with higher firm performance. That finding qualifies any broad reading of Kaal's claim that director independence did not produce effective risk monitoring in major U.S. financial failures. The meta-analysis proposition addresses firm performance, not risk monitoring under information concealment, and it does not by itself establish causation.

entry.title: Streaming Dao As Anthropological Experiment Amp Nbsp Governance Failure As Subject 3B8618843D
